chunks: 2357 - Ibn Faḍḍāl narrated from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, who said:

I sent to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام that a brother of mine bought pigeons in al-Madīnah, and we took them with us to Makkah, performed ʿumrah, remained until hajj, then brought the pigeons out with us from Makkah to al-Kūfah. Is there anything due upon us in that?
So he said to the messenger: “I think they were wild. Tell him to slaughter one sheep in place of each bird.”

key_terms.حَمَامًا: pigeons that were purchased and later taken from Makkah
key_terms.شَاةً: a sheep, the prescribed compensation for each bird
key_terms.فُرْهَةً: wild or untamed, indicating non-domesticated birds
key_terms.مَكَّةَ: the sacred city to which they were brought
key_terms.يَذْبَحُ: he must slaughter, indicating required compensation
key_terms.ٱلْحَجِّ: the pilgrimage season during which they remained there
key_terms.ٱلْحَسَنِ: the Imam addressed in the report, Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام
key_terms.ٱلْمَدِينَةِ: the city where the pigeons were bought

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on taking wild pigeons out of Makkah’s sanctuary?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding pigeons taken out from the Haram after being brought to Makkah. Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام rules that if they were wild pigeons, compensation is due by slaughtering one sheep for each bird. The report relates to the sanctity of the Haram and the rulings connected to its protected game.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2357 - Ibn Faddal narrated from Yunus ibn Ya‘qub, who said:

I sent a message to Abu Al-Hasan (as) asking about my brother, who had purchased pigeons in Medina. We took them with us to Mecca, performed ‘Umrah, stayed until Hajj, and then brought the pigeons with us from Mecca to Kufa. Is there any obligation upon us for this?
Imam (as) replied to the messenger: "I believe they were wild pigeons. Tell him he must sacrifice one sheep for each bird."
